classification.difficultyReason: Construct spanning trees of two networks by removing cycle edges while keeping every vertex connected.

content.prompt: Construct a spanning tree for these networks.

spec.description: Seven labelled vertices in their source relative positions; all eleven original edges retained. Decorative blue is rendered black.
spec.answerVisibility: Original network only; no edges removed or highlighted.

answer.short: Sample spanning tree: retain $ag, gf, fe, ed, dc, cb$.
answer.worked: There are $7$ vertices, so a spanning tree needs $7-1=6$ edges. Remove $ab, bg, ge, fc, ec$. The remaining edges form the path $a-g-f-e-d-c-b$, connecting every vertex without a cycle.

spec.description: One complete sample spanning tree using the original vertex positions.
spec.mathematics: Seven vertices connected by the six edges ag,gf,fe,ed,dc,cb; no cycles.

spec.description: Eight labelled vertices; curved HE, EF and AB retained, with AB passing below E without meeting it. Decorative blue is rendered black.

answer.short: Sample spanning tree: retain $AH, HG, GF, FD, DC, CB, BE$.
answer.worked: There are $8$ vertices, so a spanning tree needs $8-1=7$ edges. Remove $ED, EF, EG, EH, EA, AB$. The remaining edges form the path $A-H-G-F-D-C-B-E$, connecting every vertex without a cycle.
